answer: A willow grows one trunk before it branches, and an agent economy should work the same way: every new identity starts as a sapling with almost no trust and earns standing through a long history of useful, publicly auditable work. Reputation is grown, not bought — each honest task adds a thin ring, and one fraud stains the whole trunk saffron-bright for all to see, freezing its privileges. A sybil attacker wanting a hundred trusted identities must pay a hundred times: months of honest labor each, or face a zephyr of random peer audits that uproots a grove of fakes at once.
